# Opening figures — what proved each one

**Report VR-2026-04-01** · position as at **2026-03-31** · prepared by S. Ramesh (store manager)

Every figure below is going into the opening books. This page says what proved each one, and
what that proof does not cover. Nothing here rests on the old system's own word unless it says
so in the table.

## What these proofs do NOT show

Read this part. Each check has a real limit, and none of them is a formality.

- **prices** — the shelf edge proves today's price. It says nothing about whether the price was right last month.
- **barcodes** — the scan test proves the barcodes we checked scan. It does not prove every barcode in the file is on the right product.
- **customers** — a customer confirms their own details. Nothing here finds a customer the old system lost.
- **ledgers** — the CA prepared these accounts from the same old system. A signature and double entry, not an independent source.
- **loyalty** — a customer confirms the balance, not that it was ever earned. Award double points by mistake for a year and everyone confirms the wrong figure cheerfully.
- **products** — a count confirms the products on the shelf. A product the old system held and nobody stocks would not be missed by this.
- **purchases** — a statement confirms the invoices. It cannot show a purchase nobody invoiced.
- **sales** — the bank shows what arrived. A sale rung up and pocketed at the till reaches neither the old system nor the bank, and the two agree perfectly about it.
- **stock** — a count proves what is on the shelf today, not what was there at the year end.
- **suppliers** — the supplier confirms what they think we owe. It does not prove the goods were ever delivered.
- **tax** — a filed return shows what was declared, never what was correctly charged. Sold at 5% what should have been 12%, the books and the return record the same mistake.

## What needs doing

- **batches** — the printed stock report has no batch column, so nothing outside the old system can confirm batches. Book a count that records batch codes, or carry them on the old system's word.
- **prices** — 14 shelf prices differ from the extracted price file. Each is listed by product — settle them against the shelf edge before go-live.

## Exceptions the owner has accepted

Each of these is a figure carried into the opening books **on the old system's word alone.**
Each was accepted on its own, by name, with a reason.

- **batches** — accepted by R. Chezhian on 2026-04-01: *"the old system never printed batch codes on any report. We are carrying them forward unverified and will rebuild batch truth from goods-in from 1 April onward. Discussed with the CA on 28 March."*

## Signatures

- **R. Chezhian** (owner), 2026-04-02 — *"I have read the figures, the limits and the one exception above, and I accept them"*

### Why each of these records is worth believing

- **bank statement** — the bank has no interest in agreeing with our old system
- **CA's prepared accounts** — prepared independently and signed, by somebody with a licence at stake
- **customer confirmation** — the customer can see their own points balance and will say if it is wrong
- **filed GST return** — already filed, dated and signed — it cannot be adjusted to make a total agree
- **payment settlement** — the provider settled real money and their file says how much
- **physical count** — the only truth about stock that exists anywhere; everything else is a record of it
- **supplier statement** — the supplier keeps their own ledger and will confirm it, because they want paying
